## Summary

Switch only the Linux ARM64 SuperPMI collection container from Ubuntu 24.04 to `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet-buildtools/prereqs:azurelinux-4.0-helix-arm64v8`, pinned to the published manifest digest `sha256:8329f796bc5f5b0f83701139a10b6048102b8ea0f774be5e8ba8b956cee4dda0`. Update the public/internal descriptive queue aliases to `AzureLinux.4.Arm64[.Open]` and document the distinction between the collection container and its host.

The underlying Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 Helix host queue strings remain unchanged. ARM32's Debian 12 container/payload, x64 SuperPMI, other OSes, shared build images, and devcontainers are unchanged.

Related to [#136313](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/136313), specifically the S2 container-image change. This does not close the tracking issue, migrate the S1 hosts, or claim end-to-end S2 validation.

## Blockers

**Aspire signing blocks this migration:** AL4's crypto policy rejects RSA/SHA-1 signatures used by the C# compiler for full strong-name signing (`invalid digest`). A compatible signing approach is still needed; no crypto-policy change is included. This is the known compatibility problem tracked in [#65874](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/65874).

Missing `awk`/process tools are addressed separately by [dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker#1782](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker/pull/1782). This PR will need the corrected image digest after publication; the package fix does not resolve signing.

## Validation

Ran a small real collection in the exact digest-pinned image with Docker `--platform linux/arm64` on an ARM64 Docker daemon. The running container reported `aarch64` and kernel `6.10.14-linuxkit`; ELF headers for the runtime, JIT, collector shim, SuperPMI, MCS, native crossgen2, and its JIT interface were verified as ELF64 AArch64 (`e_machine=183`), not AMD64 emulation.

Reused matching public Linux ARM64 Checked Core_Root and native crossgen2 artifacts from [runtime-coreclr outerloop build 1645146](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1645146), source `bc980bc92e8093ca338810351b3db05dc073f1fa`. The repository's setup script staged and partitioned one `System.Linq.dll`, then the staged collection script ran:

```sh
python3 /validation/arm64-payload/correlation/superpmi/superpmi.py collect \
    --clean --crossgen2 \
    -assemblies /validation/arm64-payload/workitem/collectAssembliesDirectory/libraries/0/binaries \
    -arch arm64 -build_type Checked \
    -core_root /validation/arm64-payload/correlation/superpmi \
    -spmi_location /validation/spmi-cache \
    -output_mch_path /validation/collection-output/azurelinux4.linux.arm64.mch \
    -temp_dir /validation/collection-temp \
    -log_level DEBUG \
    -log_file /validation/arm64-superpmi-collection.log
```

**Passed, exit 0:** collected 1,159 method contexts and saved 1,121 after deduplication. Native MCS merge, SuperPMI cleaning, TOC generation, and final replay all succeeded. Cleaning reported `Loaded 1121  Jitted 1121  FailedCompile 0 Excluded 0 Missing 0`; final replay processed all 1,121 contexts cleanly. Produced a 9,636,084-byte MCH and 53,820-byte TOC. No packages were installed or upgraded in the image.

Also executed both baseline and modified setup code across 18 public/internal platform/architecture combinations each: **passed**, with exactly the two Linux ARM64 mappings changed and all host queues/other mappings preserved. Python compilation of the changed setup script and `git diff --check` **passed**.

Subsequent [public Helix collection build 1648090](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1648090) exercised the pinned image on the retained Ubuntu 22.04 hosts: ARM64 PMI libraries passed 6/6 workload partitions, crossgen2 libraries passed 6/6, and NativeAOT smoke passed 1/1. Benchmark/realworld SDK bootstrap failed due to missing `awk`, and Aspire failed during strong-name signing as described above.

## Limitations

- The published image identifies itself as **Azure Linux 4.0 (Container Image Beta)**.
- Local validation uses existing public runtime artifacts, not a fresh CoreCLR source build.
- Public Helix success covers the workloads listed above, not the complete collection matrix. The migration remains blocked on the package and signing issues above.
- Internal Helix queues have not been validated. The separate S1 host migration is not included.
